subject: astronomy

moments.title: Voyager 1 and 2 launch
moments.body: Voyager 2 launches on 20 August 1977; Voyager 1 on 5 September 1977. A rare planetary alignment (occurs once every 175 years) permits a gravity-assist 'Grand Tour' of the outer planets. Voyager 1 flies past Jupiter (1979), Saturn (1980). Voyager 2 also visits Uranus (1986) and Neptune (1989) — still the only spacecraft to do so.
moments.takeaway: Two spacecraft, designed for 5-year missions, are now in interstellar space (Voyager 1 in 2012, Voyager 2 in 2018) and still returning data nearly 50 years later.

moments.title: Pale Blue Dot
moments.body: On 14 February 1990, at Sagan's urging, Voyager 1 turns its camera back at the solar system from 6 billion km away. Earth appears as a sub-pixel dot — the 'Pale Blue Dot'. Sagan's 1994 reflection becomes one of the most-quoted passages in popular science.

quote.text: On it everyone you love, everyone you know, everyone you ever heard of, every human being who ever was, lived out their lives.

moments.takeaway: The view of Earth from 6 billion km redefined every framing of human conflict.

now.title: Outer planet exploration today
now.body: Galileo (Jupiter 1995-2003), Cassini-Huygens (Saturn 1997-2017), New Horizons (Pluto 2015), Juno (Jupiter 2016-), Europa Clipper (launched 2024), JUICE (launched 2023). Cassini's controlled plunge into Saturn (15 September 2017) ended an extraordinary mission.
now.open_questions: What is under Europa's ice? Could Enceladus's plumes carry life out for sampling? Missions are being designed.

reflection: Each Voyager carries a Golden Record: greetings in 55 languages, music from Bach to Chuck Berry, sounds of Earth. The records will outlast the Sun. We sent a love letter to the universe without knowing if anyone could read it.
